verification_notes: Audited from first principles: Submerged right-angled prism TIR example verified. Prism index n_g = 1.5 = 3/2, water ambient n_w = 4/3. Vertex A = 90 degrees, vertex B = theta, vertex C = 90 - theta. Ray enters face AB at normal incidence i = 0 => r = 0, ray proceeds horizontally without deviation. Geometry at hypotenuse face AC: face AC is inclined at angle theta to vertical face AB; normal to AC is inclined at angle theta to horizontal ray => incident angle theta_1 = theta. Critical angle for glass-water boundary: sin(theta_c) = n_w / n_g = (4/3) / (3/2) = 8/9 approx 0.8889 => theta_c = arcsin(8/9) approx 62.73 degrees. Condition for TIR at face AC: theta_1 > theta_c => sin(theta) > 8/9 (or theta > arcsin(8/9)). Dimensional homogeneity: sin(theta) is dimensionless, angles in degrees/radians. Limiting cases audited: air immersion sin(theta_c) = 2/3 (water immersion raises theta_c, making TIR harder); 8/9 < 1 ensures a real physical angle exists. All calculations verified.
